Documento(s) de cenário:
--- Project Scenario 6.pdf ---
SLCCI (Sea Level Climate Change Initiative)
So here's the deal — this is part of a bigger ESA effort, the Climate Change Initiative,
where they're trying to finally make proper use of thirty-plus years of Earth observation
archives instead of letting all that satellite data just sit there. There are about eleven of
these projects running in parallel, each one looking at a different climate variable, and ours
is the sea level one. Basically the science side has already been doing the heavy lifting —
building the algorithms, validating them, running a kind of prototype production setup —
and now we're at the point where somebody needs to take that prototype and turn it into
something that actually runs operationally, day in day out, and can be handed over to the
people who need the data.
What I picture happening is a system that pulls in altimetry data from a bunch of different
satellite missions, runs it through calibration and validation, cross-calibrates between
missions so everything is consistent, and spits out two kinds of products: one is like a
per-mission track of measurements, and the other is a merged, gridded product that blends
all the missions together into one consistent climate record. On top of that there needs to
be a proper archive, because reprocessing is going to happen again and again as
algorithms improve or new calibration methods come out, so we can't afford to lose the
baseline data or any of the intermediate stuff along the way.
The people using this thing day-to-day are going to be on two very different sides.
Internally you've got the folks who actually run and maintain the production line —
scientists who get pulled in when something needs deeper validation or when a new
product has to be defined, people who just judge and sign off on product quality, people
who handle the catalog and metadata, and then the more operational crowd who monitor
the system, handle incidents, deal with user requests, that sort of thing. Externally, the
audience is really the climate research community — people doing climate modelling work
who just want reliable, well-documented sea level data they can trust and build on. We're
not building this for the general public or commercial customers, it's a fairly specialized
research crowd.
One thing I want to be upfront about: we don't need to worry about near-real-time delivery.
There's a whole separate world of oceanographic services that care about getting data out
within hours for things like operational forecasting, and that's just not us — we're purely
about delayed-time and the long, reprocessed historical series for climate purposes, so
anything geared at that fast-turnaround NRT use case can be dropped from consideration
entirely. Similarly, all that formal IT service management process stuff, incident ticketing
frameworks and so on, isn't something we need to bring in here, it just doesn't fit how this
is going to be run.
Cost is a real concern too, this has to be something that's sustainable to operate long term,
not just a one-off build. And it has to be flexible — new satellite missions are coming online

during the life of the project and the algorithms themselves are going to keep changing as
the science matures, so whatever gets built can't be rigid, it needs to absorb new data
sources and let people swap in improved processing logic without everything falling apart.
There's also a push to not reinvent the wheel — there's existing infrastructure out there
already doing something very similar for ocean data more broadly, and wherever it makes
sense we'd rather lean on what's proven and working than build everything from a blank
page. Quality and traceability of the data matter a lot too, since the whole point is feeding
trustworthy numbers into the international climate change conversation, so whatever
comes out the other end needs solid metadata and documentation attached, not just raw
numbers.

Sistema: SLCCI (Sea Level Climate Change Initiative)

Resumo executivo: SLCCI is an operational delayed-time sea-level climate-data production system within the ESA Climate Change Initiative. It transforms multi-mission satellite altimetry archives into calibrated, validated, cross-calibrated, documented, and traceable sea-level products for climate research, while preserving all source and intermediate data required for future reprocessing.

Escopo: The system ingests, processes, archives, documents, and distributes delayed-time sea-level climate products derived from satellite altimetry missions.
  Em escopo: Ingestion of altimetry data from multiple satellite missions
  Em escopo: Calibration, validation, and cross-calibration of mission data
  Em escopo: Generation of per-mission track products
  Em escopo: Generation of merged gridded climate products
  Em escopo: Archiving of source, intermediate, and generated product data
  Em escopo: Reprocessing using updated algorithms or calibration methods
  Em escopo: Cataloguing, metadata management, product documentation, and quality approval
  Em escopo: Operational monitoring and handling of operational user requests
  Fora de escopo: Near-real-time data delivery — the initiative is limited to delayed-time and historical climate products
  Fora de escopo: Operational oceanographic forecasting — it belongs to separate oceanographic services
  Fora de escopo: Public-oriented services — the target audience is the specialized climate research community
  Fora de escopo: Commercial customer services — the initiative is not intended for commercial users
  Fora de escopo: Formal IT service-management ticketing frameworks — they are explicitly excluded from the operating model
  Premissa: PA-01: Satellite altimetry source data from participating missions will be available for ingestion.
  Premissa: PA-02: Scientific teams will provide validated processing algorithms, calibration methods, and product definitions.
  Premissa: PA-03: Existing ocean-data infrastructure can be assessed for reuse where it meets SLCCI operational needs. [INFERRED]
  Premissa: PA-04: Climate researchers will access distributed products and their accompanying metadata through an interface to be defined. [TBD]
  Restrição: REST-01 (Operational scope): The system shall support delayed-time and historical reprocessed data only; near-real-time delivery is excluded.
  Restrição: REST-02 (Cost): The solution shall be sustainable for long-term operation; the operational cost ceiling is [TBD].
  Restrição: REST-03 (Adaptability): The solution shall accommodate future satellite missions and evolving processing algorithms.
  Restrição: REST-04 (Reuse): Existing proven ocean-data infrastructure shall be reused where technically suitable.

Stakeholders:
  STK-01 - Production and maintenance personnel (Usuário primário): Operate production workflows, monitor processing execution, investigate operational conditions, and maintain the processing environment.
  STK-02 - Sea-level scientists (Usuário primário): Perform deeper validation, define new products, provide updated algorithms, and assess scientific processing outputs.
  STK-03 - Product quality assessors (Usuário primário): Review product-quality evidence and approve or reject product releases.
  STK-04 - Catalogue and metadata managers (Usuário primário): Manage product catalogue records, metadata, documentation, and data traceability information.
  STK-05 - Operations personnel (Usuário primário): Monitor the operational service, handle incidents outside formal ITSM frameworks, and respond to user requests.
  STK-06 - Climate modelling researchers (Usuário secundário): Discover and obtain reliable, documented, traceable sea-level climate products for climate research and modelling.
  STK-07 - ESA Climate Change Initiative (Stakeholder externo): Receive sustainable operational sea-level climate-data production that contributes to the wider Climate Change Initiative.

Regras de negócio:
  RN-001 - Delayed-time climate-data focus: Sea-level products are produced for delayed-time climate research and long-term historical records, not for near-real-time operational forecasting.
  RN-002 - Product types: The initiative provides a per-mission measurement-track product and a merged gridded product combining consistent measurements from multiple missions.
  RN-003 - Reprocessing preservation: Baseline data and all processing intermediates must be preserved because historical products are reprocessed when algorithms or calibration methods evolve.
  RN-004 - Quality release approval: A product must be assessed and signed off by designated quality assessors before being released to climate researchers.
  RN-005 - Traceable product information: Distributed climate products must include metadata and documentation sufficient to identify their source data, processing provenance, and quality context.

Requisitos funcionais:
  RF-001 - Ingest mission altimetry data: The system shall ingest altimetry data supplied by each configured satellite mission. [Must have]
  RF-002 - Calibrate mission data: The system shall apply the configured calibration method to ingested altimetry data. [Must have]
  RF-003 - Validate processed data: The system shall record the result of validation performed against the configured validation rules for each processed dataset. [Must have]
  RF-004 - Cross-calibrate mission datasets: The system shall apply the configured cross-calibration method to datasets selected from multiple satellite missions. [Must have]
  RF-005 - Generate mission-track product: The system shall generate a per-mission measurement-track product from processed data of one satellite mission. [Must have]
  RF-006 - Generate merged gridded product: The system shall generate a merged gridded sea-level product from cross-calibrated datasets of multiple satellite missions. [Must have]
  RF-007 - Archive processing artefacts: The system shall archive each source dataset, intermediate processing dataset, and generated product with its processing version. [Must have]
  RF-008 - Reprocess historical data: The system shall execute a reprocessing run for selected archived datasets using a selected processing version. [Must have]
  RF-009 - Manage product metadata: The system shall associate source-data identifiers, processing-version identifiers, validation results, and documentation references with each generated product. [Must have]
  RF-010 - Approve product release: The system shall record a quality assessor's approval or rejection decision for each generated product. [Must have]
  RF-011 - Provide approved products: The system shall make a product available to climate researchers only when its recorded quality decision is approved. [Must have]
  RF-012 - Configure satellite mission source: The system shall allow authorized production personnel to register a new satellite mission as a data source. [Should have]
  RF-013 - Configure processing version: The system shall allow authorized scientists to register a new processing algorithm or calibration-method version. [Should have]
  RF-014 - Monitor production runs: The system shall display the execution status of each production and reprocessing run. [Should have]

Requisitos não funcionais:
  RNF-001 (Reliability) - The system shall verify the integrity of 100% of archived source, intermediate, and generated files through a stored checksum at archival time and at each retrieval. | Métrica: 100% of archived files have a checksum, and 100% of retrievals verify a matching checksum.
  RNF-002 (Functional Suitability) - The system shall provide complete provenance metadata for 100% of externally released products, including source-data identifiers, processing-version identifier, validation result, and documentation reference. | Métrica: 100% of released products contain the four specified provenance fields.
  RNF-003 (Performance Efficiency) - The system shall complete a reprocessing run for one configured mission dataset within 24 hours. [TBD] | Métrica: A representative mission dataset completes with final status 'Completed' within 24 hours of run initiation. [TBD]
  RNF-004 (Reliability) - The system shall provide at least 99.0% monthly availability for production monitoring, catalogue access, and product-distribution functions, excluding planned maintenance. [TBD] | Métrica: Monthly availability is at least 99.0%, measured over each calendar month. [TBD]
  RNF-005 (Flexibility) - The system shall support onboarding one new satellite mission through configuration and integration activities without modifying the processing core source code. [TBD] | Métrica: One new mission is ingested and processed successfully with zero source-code changes to the processing core. [TBD]
  RNF-006 (Maintainability) - The system shall execute the automated regression suite with at least 90% pass rate after registration of a new processing version. [TBD] | Métrica: At least 90% of automated regression tests pass for each registered processing version. [TBD]
  RNF-007 (Compatibility) - The system shall exchange 100% of required datasets and metadata with each approved reused ocean-data infrastructure interface using its agreed interface specification. [TBD] | Métrica: 100% of mandatory interface test cases pass for each approved integration. [TBD]

Histórias de usuário:
  HU-001 - Como production operator, quero ingest data from a configured satellite mission, para start the delayed-time production workflow
  HU-002 - Como sea-level scientist, quero apply a defined calibration method to mission data, para obtain scientifically consistent measurements
  HU-003 - Como sea-level scientist, quero review recorded validation results, para assess whether processed data satisfies defined validation rules
  HU-004 - Como sea-level scientist, quero cross-calibrate datasets from multiple missions, para produce a consistent multi-mission climate record
  HU-005 - Como climate modelling researcher, quero obtain a per-mission measurement-track product, para analyse sea-level observations from a specific mission
  HU-006 - Como climate modelling researcher, quero obtain a merged gridded sea-level product, para use a consistent climate record in climate-modelling research
  HU-007 - Como catalogue and metadata manager, quero retain all processing artefacts by processing version, para support reproducibility and future reprocessing
  HU-008 - Como sea-level scientist, quero reprocess archived datasets with an updated processing version, para produce improved historical climate products
  HU-009 - Como catalogue and metadata manager, quero attach provenance and documentation to each product, para allow researchers to assess product origin and processing context
  HU-010 - Como product quality assessor, quero record an approval decision for a product, para control release of quality-assessed products
  HU-011 - Como climate modelling researcher, quero access approved products, para use products that have passed the defined quality process
  HU-012 - Como production operator, quero register a new satellite mission, para incorporate future observation sources into production
  HU-013 - Como sea-level scientist, quero register an updated processing version, para apply improved scientific logic in future production runs
  HU-014 - Como operations personnel member, quero view production-run statuses, para identify runs requiring operational intervention

Casos de uso:
  UC-001 - Run delayed-time product production | Ator: Production operator
    1. The production operator selects a configured satellite mission and source dataset.
    2. The system ingests the selected altimetry data.
    3. The system applies the configured calibration method.
    4. The system records the validation result.
    5. The system generates the applicable product.
    6. The system archives the production artefacts.
  UC-002 - Reprocess archived data | Ator: Sea-level scientist
    1. The sea-level scientist selects archived datasets.
    2. The sea-level scientist selects a registered processing version.
    3. The system creates a reprocessing run.
    4. The system processes the selected datasets using the selected version.
    5. The system archives the resulting artefacts with the processing version.
  UC-003 - Approve and distribute product | Ator: Product quality assessor
    1. The product quality assessor selects a generated product.
    2. The system displays its validation results and metadata.
    3. The assessor records an approval decision.
    4. The system records status 'Approved'.
    5. The system makes the approved product available to climate modelling researchers.
  UC-004 - Configure a new mission source | Ator: Production operator
    1. The production operator enters the new satellite mission configuration.
    2. The system validates the required configuration fields.
    3. The system registers the mission as a data source.
    4. The system confirms the source registration.
  UC-005 - Monitor production runs | Ator: Operations personnel member
    1. The operations personnel member opens the production-run monitor.
    2. The system lists production and reprocessing runs.
    3. The system displays the execution status for each listed run.
    4. The actor reviews the displayed statuses.

Critérios de aceite:
  CA-001 - Dado a configured satellite mission and an available source dataset, quando a production operator starts ingestion for that dataset, então the system records the dataset with ingestion status 'Completed'.
  CA-002 - Dado an ingested dataset and a configured calibration method, quando the system processes the dataset, então the resulting dataset contains the identifier of the applied calibration method.
  CA-003 - Dado a calibrated dataset and configured validation rules, quando the system executes validation, então the dataset has a recorded validation status of 'Passed' or 'Failed'.
  CA-004 - Dado processed datasets from two configured satellite missions, quando a scientist starts cross-calibration, então the system creates a cross-calibrated dataset containing both mission identifiers.
  CA-005 - Dado processed data from one satellite mission, quando the system generates a mission-track product, então the generated product is identified as a per-mission measurement-track product and contains one mission identifier.
  CA-006 - Dado a cross-calibrated dataset from multiple missions, quando the system generates a merged gridded product, então the generated product is identified as a merged gridded product and contains at least two mission identifiers.
  CA-007 - Dado a completed production run, quando the system archives its artefacts, então the source dataset, each intermediate dataset, and the generated product are retrievable with a processing-version identifier.
  CA-008 - Dado an archived dataset and a registered processing version, quando a scientist starts a reprocessing run, então the system creates a new product version and preserves the original archived dataset.
  CA-009 - Dado a generated product, quando the system registers its metadata, então the product metadata contains source-data identifiers, a processing-version identifier, a validation result, and a documentation reference.
  CA-010 - Dado a generated product with validation results and metadata, quando a product quality assessor records an approval or rejection decision, então the system stores the decision as status 'Approved' or 'Rejected' with the assessor identifier.
  CA-011 - Dado one product with status 'Approved' and one product with status 'Rejected', quando a climate modelling researcher requests the products, então the system provides the approved product and denies access to the rejected product.
  CA-012 - Dado an authorized production operator and valid mission configuration data, quando the operator submits the new mission configuration, então the system creates a unique mission-source identifier with status 'Configured'.
  CA-013 - Dado an authorized scientist and a new algorithm or calibration-method version, quando the scientist submits the version, então the system registers a unique processing-version identifier.
  CA-014 - Dado production and reprocessing runs with recorded statuses, quando operations personnel open the production-run monitor, então the system displays each run identifier and one status value: 'Queued', 'Running', 'Completed', or 'Failed'.

Glossário:
  Altimetry data: Satellite observation data used to derive sea-level measurements.
  Delayed-time: Data-production mode intended for quality-controlled climate records rather than delivery within hours of observation.
  Per-mission measurement-track product: A sea-level product containing measurements associated with one satellite mission track.
  Merged gridded product: A gridded sea-level climate product created by combining cross-calibrated measurements from multiple satellite missions.
  Cross-calibration: Processing activity that makes measurements from different satellite missions consistent with one another.
  Processing version: Identified version of an algorithm, calibration method, or processing logic used to generate a dataset or product.
  Reprocessing: Execution of processing on archived historical data using a selected updated processing version.
  Provenance metadata: Metadata that identifies the source data, processing version, validation result, and documentation associated with a product.

O Documento de Especificação de Requisitos de Software (SRS) é o contrato técnico que descreve o 
que o sistema deve fazer e sob quais condições de qualidade. Ele serve de referência para 
desenvolvedores, testadores, gerentes e clientes durante todo o ciclo de vida do projeto.
1.1 Artefatos Obrigatórios e sua Ordem
Um SRS completo e formal deve conter os seguintes artefatos, nesta ordem:
• ESCOPO: Define o que está DENTRO e FORA do projeto. Evita scope creep.
• STAKEHOLDERS: Lista todos os envolvidos: quem usa, quem financia, quem é afetado.
• PREMISSAS E RESTRIÇÕES: Fatos assumidos como verdadeiros e limites impostos ao projeto.
• REGRAS DE NEGÓCIO (RN): Políticas, fórmulas e condições de negócio que existem independentemente 
do software.
• REQUISITOS FUNCIONAIS (RF): O que o sistema DEVE FAZER — comportamentos, serviços, respostas a 
entradas.
• REQUISITOS NÃO FUNCIONAIS (RNF): Como o sistema deve SER — atributos de qualidade 
quantificáveis.
• HISTÓRIAS DE USUÁRIO (HU): Necessidades na perspectiva do usuário: Como [perfil], quero [ação], para
[benefício].
• CASOS DE USO (UC): Interações detalhadas ator-sistema com fluxo principal, alternativo e exceções.
• CRITÉRIOS DE ACEITE (CA): Condições testáveis em formato BDD (Dado/Quando/Então) que definem 
quando o requisito está concluído.
• GLOSSÁRIO: Termos do domínio com definição precisa para eliminar ambiguidades.
1.2 Como os Artefatos se Interconectam
Os artefatos formam uma cadeia de rastreabilidade. Cada RF deve ter origem em um STK 
(stakeholder) ou RN. Cada HU deve ter pelo menos um RF associado. Cada RF e HU devem ter pelo menos um CA. Esta rastreabilidade garante que nada seja implementado sem justificativa de 
negócio e que tudo que foi prometido seja testável.
Cadeia de rastreabilidade mínima:
STK → (RN →) RF → HU → CA

A ISO/IEC 25010:2023 define 9 características de qualidade do produto. Todo RNF deve ser 
classificado em uma dessas características. A seguir, cada característica com seus sub-atributos e 
exemplo de RNF.
1. Functional Suitability (Adequação Funcional)
 Functional Completeness — o sistema oferece todas as funções necessárias.
 Functional Correctness — as funções produzem os resultados corretos.
 Functional Appropriateness — as funções facilitam a realização das tarefas.
EXEMPLO — RNF — 1. Functional Suitability
O sistema deve calcular o imposto sobre o valor do pedido aplicando corretamente a alíquota de ICMS 
vigente para o estado de destino, conforme tabela oficial CONFAZ, com variação máxima de R$ 0,01 em 
relação ao valor de referência da Receita Estadual.
2. Performance Efficiency (Eficiência de Desempenho)
 Time Behaviour — tempo de resposta e throughput.
 Resource Utilisation — uso de CPU, memória, rede.
 Capacity — limites máximos suportados.
EXEMPLO — RNF — 2. Performance Efficiency
O sistema deve processar no mínimo 200 pedidos por minuto sob carga de 1.000 usuários simultâneos, com 
tempo de resposta inferior a 2 segundos no percentil 95.
3. Compatibility (Compatibilidade)
 Co-existence — coexiste com outros sistemas sem degradação.
 Interoperability — troca dados com outros sistemas.
EXEMPLO — RNF — 3. Compatibility
A API do sistema deve expor endpoints REST/JSON compatíveis com o padrão OpenAPI 3.0, permitindo 
integração com o ERP legado via OAuth 2.0 sem modificações no ERP.4. Interaction Capability (Capacidade de Interação) — antes 'Usabilidade'
 Appropriateness Recognisability — usuário reconhece a adequação do sistema.
 Learnability — facilidade de aprendizado.
 Operability — facilidade de operação.
 User Error Protection — proteção contra erros do usuário.
 User Engagement — interface envolvente e motivadora.
 Inclusivity — acessível a pessoas com diferentes capacidades.

When old requirements don’t exist
Most older systems do not have documented—let alone accurate—requirements. In the absence of 
reliable documentation, teams might reverse-engineer an understanding of what the system does 
from the user interfaces, code, and database. We think of this as “software archaeology.” To maximize 
the benefit from reverse engineering, the archaeology expedition should record what it learns in 
the form of requirements and design descriptions. Accumulating accurate information about certain 
portions of the current system positions the team to enhance a system with low risk, to replace a 
system without missing critical functionality, and to perform future enhancements efficiently. It halts 
the knowledge drain, so future maintainers better understand the changes that were just made.
If updating the requirements is overly burdensome, it will fall by the wayside as busy people rush 
on to the next change request. Obsolete requirements aren’t helpful for future enhancements. There’s 
a widespread fear in the software industry that writing documentation will consume too much time; 
the knee-jerk reaction is to neglect all opportunities to update requirements documentation. But 
what’s the cost if you don’t update the requirements and a future maintainer (perhaps you!) has to 
regenerate that information? The answer to this question will let you make a thoughtful business 
decision concerning whether to revise the requirements documentation when you change or 
re-create the software.
When the team performs additional enhancements and maintenance over time, it can extend 
these fractional knowledge representations, steadily improving the system documentation. The 
incremental cost of recording this newly found knowledge is small compared with the cost of 
someone having to rediscover it later on. Implementing enhancements almost always necessitates 
further requirements development, so add those new requirements to an existing requirements 
repository, if there is one. If you’re replacing an old system, you have an opportunity to document 
the requirements for the new one and to keep the requirements up to date with what you learn 
throughout the project. Try to leave the requirements in better shape than you found them.
Which requirements should you specify?
It’s not always worth taking the time to generate a complete set of requirements for an entire 
production system. Many options lie between the two extremes of continuing forever with no 
requirements documentation and reconstructing a perfect requirements set. Knowing why you’d like 
to have written requirements available lets you judge whether the cost of rebuilding all—or even 
part—of the specification is a sound investment.

Level of detail
One of the biggest challenges is determining the appropriate level of detail at which to document 
requirements gleaned from the existing system. For enhancements, defining requirements for the 
new functionality alone might be sufficient. However, you will usually benefit from documenting all of 
the functionality that closely relates to the enhancement, to ensure that the change fits in seamlessly 
(region B in Figure 21-2). You might want to create business processes, user requirements, and/or 
functional requirements for those related areas. For example, let’s say you are adding a discount code 
feature to an existing shopping cart function, but you don’t have any documented requirements for 
the shopping cart. You might be tempted to write just a single user story: “As a customer, I need to be 
able to enter a discount code so I can get the cheapest price for the product.” However, this user story 
alone lacks context, so consider capturing other user stories about shopping cart operations. That 
information could be valuable the next time you need to modify the shopping cart function.
I worked with one team that was just beginning to develop the requirements for version 2 of 
a major product with embedded software. They hadn’t done a good job on the requirements for 
version 1, which was currently being implemented. The lead BA wondered, “Is it worth going back 
to improve the SRS for version 1?” The company anticipated that this product line would be a major 
revenue generator for at least 10 years. They also planned to reuse some of the core requirements 
in several spin-off products. In this case, it made sense to improve the requirements documentation 
for version 1 because it was the foundation for all subsequent development work in this product line.

SRS described just the differences that the new version should exhibit compared to the previous 
version. Nowhere was there a description of the original system. Consequently, everyone had a 
different understanding of the current system’s capabilities. If you’re in this situation, document 
the requirements for your project more thoroughly so that all the stakeholders—both present 
and future—understand what the system does.
Expected challenges
The presence of an existing system leads to common challenges that both enhancement and 
replacement projects will face, including the following:
■ The changes made could degrade the performance to which users are accustomed.
■ Little or no requirements documentation might be available for the existing system.
■ Users who are familiar with how the system works today might not like the changes they are 
about to encounter.
■ You might unknowingly break or omit functionality that is vital to some stakeholder group.
■ Stakeholders might take this opportunity to request new functionality that seems like a good 
idea but isn’t really needed to meet the business objectives.
Even if there is existing documentation, it might not prove useful. For enhancement projects, 
the documentation might not be up to date. If the documentation doesn’t match the existing 
application’s reality, it is of limited use. For replacement systems, you also need to be wary of carrying 
forward all of the requirements, because some of the old functionality probably should not be 
migrated.
One of the major issues in replacement projects is validating that the reasons for the replacement 
are sound. There need to be justifiable business objectives for the change. When existing systems 
are being completely replaced, organizational processes might also have to change, which makes it 
harder for people to accept a new system. The change in business processes, change in the software 
system, and learning curve of a new system can disrupt current operations.

GABARITO — Project Scenario 6: SLCCI (Sea Level Climate Change Initiative)
Use: "ground_truth" field for RAGAS (context_precision / context_recall).
Each line is an atomic, checkable claim against the scenario text and the
knowledge base — not a full SRS, just the set of facts a well-grounded SRS
for this scenario should be able to cover.

- The system is part of ESA's Climate Change Initiative (CCI), one of about eleven parallel projects each covering a different climate variable.
- The system must take an existing science prototype/production setup and turn it into an operational, day-to-day system.
- The system ingests altimetry data from multiple satellite missions.
- The system performs calibration, validation, and cross-calibration between missions.
- The system produces two product types: a per-mission along-track product and a merged multi-mission gridded product.
- The system must include an archive to preserve baseline and intermediate data, since reprocessing will happen repeatedly.
- Internal users include scientists (deeper validation/product definition), quality reviewers who sign off on products, catalog/metadata staff, and operational staff (monitoring, incidents, user requests).
- External users are the climate research community, not the general public or commercial customers.
- Near-real-time (NRT) delivery is explicitly out of scope; the system is delayed-time / reprocessed-data only.
- Formal IT service management processes and incident ticketing frameworks (e.g. ITIL-style) are explicitly out of scope.
- The system must be cost-sustainable to operate long-term, not just a one-off build.
- The system must be flexible enough to absorb new satellite missions and updated processing algorithms over time.
- The system should reuse existing proven infrastructure rather than being built entirely from scratch.
- Output data must include solid metadata and documentation to ensure quality and traceability.

The system must perform calibration and validation of ingested altimetry data.
The system must perform cross-calibration between different satellite missions to ensure consistency.
The system must generate the per-mission along-track product.
The system must generate the merged multi-mission gridded product, blending data from multiple missions into a single climate record.
The system must archive baseline and intermediate data to support future reprocessing without loss.
The system must allow scientists to perform deeper validation or define new products when needed.
The system must allow quality reviewers to evaluate and sign off on products before release.
The system must maintain a catalog with metadata for generated products.
The system must allow operational staff to monitor the system, handle incidents, and respond to user requests.
The system must attach metadata and documentation to output data, ensuring quality and traceability.
The system must support onboarding new satellite missions over time.
The system must support swapping in updated processing algorithms without interrupting existing operations.

historias_de_usuario.descricao: As a scientist, I want to perform deeper validation or define new products when needed, so that scientific quality is maintained as the system evolves.
As a quality reviewer, I want to evaluate and approve products, so that only validated data is released.
As a member of the catalog/metadata team, I want to maintain the product catalog and metadata, so that the data stays discoverable and well-documented.
As a member of the operational staff, I want to monitor the system, handle incidents, and respond to user requests, so that day-to-day operations keep running.
As a climate research community member, I want to access reliable, well-documented sea level data, so that I can trust it and build my research on it.

As a system operator, I want to reprocess historical data when algorithms or calibration methods improve, without losing baseline or intermediate data, so that the climate record stays accurate over time.

casos_de_uso.descricao: Process satellite altimetry data — the system ingests data from multiple missions, calibrates and validates it, cross-calibrates between missions, and generates the per-mission and multi-mission gridded products.
Review and release product — a quality reviewer evaluates a newly generated product and approves it for release, or flags it for correction.
Reprocess historical data — an operator triggers reprocessing of archived baseline/intermediate data using an updated algorithm or calibration method, without losing prior data.
Onboard new satellite mission — an operator or scientist configures the system to ingest data from a newly available satellite mission.

criterios_de_aceite.descricao: Given altimetry data from two or more satellite missions, when cross-calibration is performed, then the resulting measurements are consistent across missions.
Given a reprocessing run using an updated algorithm, when processing completes, then the baseline and intermediate data from previous runs remain intact and accessible.
Given a newly generated product, when a quality reviewer evaluates it, then the product is approved for release or flagged for correction.
Given a released dataset, when a climate research community member accesses it, then the dataset includes metadata and documentation sufficient to trace its origin and processing history.
Given a new satellite mission becomes available, when it is onboarded, then that mission's data is processed without requiring a rebuild of the existing processing pipelines.
